# BS Report: "The Only 14 Ways to Make Money with AI in 2026"

**Source:** Dan Martell, YouTube, 2026-04-30 · 1,164,773 views · 35,085 likes · 2.93M subscribers · fetched 2026-07-27
**BS score: 5/10 — real tools, real trends, guru math, and a funnel every four minutes.**

*Generated by the [bullshit-detector](../../skills/analysis/bullshit-detector/SKILL.md) skill.*

## What it says (neutral summary)

Martell ranks 14 ways to make money with AI into S/A/B/F tiers by profitability, competition, and longevity: voice agents, lead generation, faceless YouTube channels, content repurposing, consulting, virtual assistants, chat agents, trading bots, agent development, copywriting, venture studios, AI-to-AI marketplaces, logo/brand design, and managed cybersecurity. He rates agent development as the top opportunity and closes with a five-step launch playbook (validate → pre-sell → deliver manually → partner for audience → productize).

## Hype signals observed

- **Urgency/scarcity:** "That's the window we're in right now" [00:00]; "things… will literally fall off a cliff in the near future" [01:04]
- **Absolutes:** "The **only** 14 ways"; "the **only real** ways to make money with AI" [00:00]; "Interfaces are dead, okay?" [10:27]
- **n=1 anecdotes as market research:** pricing validated by "I talked to my barber" [01:04]; "my friend Hunter… was getting paid to generate leads" [03:09]
- **Unverifiable self-credentials:** "launches a new AI company every single month, most of which are making millions" [00:00]
- **Funnel density — four in 26 minutes:** "Sell by Chat Playbook" via Instagram DM [05:16]; Apex "click the link below" [08:23–09:25]; book plug ("as the guy who wrote Buy Back Your Time") [08:23]; text-script lead magnet + closing DM call-to-action [23:09, 26:18]
- **Preemptive flattery/reassurance replacing evidence:** "you're not behind… you just might have been following the wrong map" [26:18]
- **Social proof as proof:** "companies know, just look at the comments below" [07:20]

## Incentive analysis

The video is top-of-funnel for Martell's ecosystem: the Instagram-DM "playbook" builds a sales-conversation list, Apex gets a mid-video product placement dressed as a tier review, and his book and venture studio get authority-building mentions. His #1 pick (agent development) is exactly the market Apex sells into — rating it "the S of the S of the S" and then offering himself as the guide is a clean conflict of interest. Notably, he *discloses* several conflicts ("I have a dog in the fight", "I'm an investor in Intercom"), which is more than most in the genre.

## Bottom line

This is competent hype, not a scam. Every tool and company named is real, two genuinely predatory ideas (faceless channels, trading bots) are correctly called out, and the validate-before-build launch sequence is standard, sane advice. What earns the 5/10: checkable facts are consistently stretched one notch (employee-only hedge funds ×3, marketplace stats from the marketplace's own PR, a rival protocol recast as "jumping on board"), income figures are anecdotes with no failure rates or timelines, and the whole piece funnels toward paid products whose value depends on you believing the framing. Treat the tier list as one practitioner's marketing-tinted map, ignore the dollar figures, and note that "which one I'd pick" is also "which one I sell."
